items.titleEn: ‘Very bizarre action' as gold retraces entire summer rally to test $4,000/oz: AI weakness, or yen intervention? – Jesse Columbo
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold’s dramatic Thursday selloff Has erased all of the yellow metals gains since the summer, and the lack of correlation with the US dollar index and bond yields suggests that this could be more than liquidations from the tech selloff, and may indicate the next round of yen interventions by the U.S. government, according to Jesse Colombo, independent precious metals analyst and founder of the BubbleBubble Report. Columbo told Kitco News on Thursday afternoon that he was just trying to decipher what was going on in the gold market. “Very bizarre action,” he said. “The dollar index is down. Normally you would expect the dollar index to be up one percent on a day like this, and yet it's down 15 basis points.”

Gold and silver are not the best inflation hedges; investors should diversify into the commodity supercycle – Auspice Capital
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Gold ’s disappointing performance in recent months is further proof that it is not a reliable inflation hedge, and while it remains an important diversification tool, one fund manager says investors should be looking at broad-based exposure to commodities as the global economy enters what could be a generational supercycle. In an interview with Kitco News, Tim Pickering, President and CIO of Auspice Capital Advisors, said that while he personally likes gold and silver , he would not be investing in the precious metals at this time, as persistent inflation and elevated interest rates continue to create significant headwinds. Pickering explained that gold's biggest weakness as an inflation hedge is that it can become a rate-sensitive investment precisely when consumers are facing rising prices. He noted that this is not the first time gold has been a disappointing inflation hedge. He pointed out that gold struggled between 2020 and 2022, even as U.S. inflation surged to a four-decade high of 9%.
